sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Domu language (dof), combined catalog, up-to-date as of 2025-02-10 (Internet Archive copy 2025-02-11).

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds). 2026. Ethnologue: Languages of the World — 'Domu' [dof], public summary (subscription content not accessed).

sources.note: Public part: 'Domu is a stable indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family.' Vitality 'Stable', digital support 'Still'. No phonology; dialects, resources and comments are behind the subscription wall (recorded as login, not bypassed).

sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content: province, ISO code, Ethnologue link. sources.note: Nothing. Domu subsection 2.9.5.5.2 (p. 638-639) repeats the 1971 location/classification note (covers Ray 1938's Damu and Merani subdivisions of his Domu Group). No stress/accent/phonology for Domu anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Thomson, N. P. 1975. Magi phonology and grammar — fifty years afterwards. In T. E. Dutton (ed.), Studies in languages of Central and South-East Papua (Pacific Linguistics C-29), 599-666.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: For MAGI (Mailu), the sister language, not Domu: sec. 2.5 Stress, p. 605-606: 'The stress on a word is usually on the second last syllable. Although it does sometime occur on the third last syllable, it never occurs on the last syllable in a polysyllabic word'. Domu is not mentioned in the paper; this does not transfer to Domu.
sources.venue: Studies in languages of Central and South-East Papua (Pacific Linguistics C-29)

sources.citation: Thomson, N. P. 1975. The dialects of Magi. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 37-90.
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative wordlists include a Dom village (Domu) list; note 7 remarks that Magi and Domu count with a base-five system unlike other Mailuan languages. No stress marks or stress remarks.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40)

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1973. A checklist of languages and present-day villages of central and south-east mainland Papua. Pacific Linguistics B-24. Canberra: ANU.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1971. Languages of South-East Papua: a preliminary report. In T. Dutton, C. Voorhoeve & S. A. Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 1-46. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Domu section 4.42 (p. 24) gives villages (Dom, Merani, Tutubu), location and relationships (closest to Bauwaki); Mailuan intro (p. 19-20) gives lexicostatistics; App. 5.1 lists a Dom wordlist recorded 9.10.69 (tape P112, 'L,G' = lexical and grammatical data). No stress, accent or phonology remarks for any Mailuan language. (Note: the chapter-level ANU handle 1885/254299 serves a mislabeled file, the front matter of Selepet Phonology; the whole-volume handle 1885/145019 was used.)
